title: Your options, side by side
summary: When both partners carry the same condition, couples have several options. None is right for everyone; each is listed in alphabetical order with equal weight.

options.name: Continue and plan ahead
options.involves: Have a pregnancy without extra testing, and plan care with doctors so any condition is found and supported early.
questions: What care would be available for our child?

options.name: IVF with embryo testing (PGT)
options.involves: IVF treatment where embryos are tested before one is placed in the womb.
questions: How many cycles might it take?

options.name: Talk it through with a counsellor first
options.involves: A conversation with a genetic counsellor before deciding anything.
questions: What else should we know about our results?

options.name: Test during pregnancy
options.involves: Testing the pregnancy (for example CVS or amniocentesis) to learn whether the baby is affected.
questions: What are the risks of the test?

options.name: Test other family members
options.involves: Relatives can choose to be tested to understand their own chances.
questions: Who in my family might want testing?

options.name: Faith and family
options.involves: Talking with your family and a religious scholar you trust. GeneBridge does not give religious rulings.
questions: Where can we find official guidance?

sources.title: Embryo testing and treatments for disease
